   153→| `--csv-file` | | ./bandwacht_log.csv | CSV-Dateipfad |
   154→| `--verbose` | `-v` | off | Ausführliche Ausgabe |
   155→| `--debug` | | off | Debug-Ausgabe (inkl. WebSocket-Nachrichten) |
   156→
   157→### Unterstützte Bänder
   158→
   159→160m, 80m, 60m, 40m, 30m, 20m, 17m, 15m, 12m, 10m, 6m, **2m**, **70cm**, 23cm, PMR, Freenet, CB, AIS, NOAA, Airband
   160→
   161→## Multi-Instanz-Betrieb
   162→
   163→Überwache mehrere OpenWebRX-Instanzen gleichzeitig:
   164→
   165→```bash
   166→python bandwacht_multi.py --config examples/multi_instance.json
   167→```
   168→
   169→Dies ermöglicht z.B. ein verteiltes Monitoring-Netzwerk über ganz Österreich.
   170→
   171→## Architektur
   172→
   173→```
   174→┌──────────────────┐     WebSocket      ┌──────────────────┐
   175→│  OpenWebRX #1    │◄──────────────────►│                  │
   176→│  (z.B. Kärnten)  │   FFT + Audio      │                  │
   177→└──────────────────┘                    │                  │
   178→                                        │   BandWacht      │──► Console
   179→┌──────────────────┐     WebSocket      │                  │──► Gotify
   180→│  OpenWebRX #2    │◄──────────────────►│   Spectrum       │──► Telegram
   181→│  (z.B. Stmk)    │   FFT + Audio      │   Analyzer       │──► ntfy
   182→└──────────────────┘                    │                  │──► Webhook
   183→                                        │                  │──► WAV Recording
   184→┌──────────────────┐     WebSocket      │                  │──► CSV Log
   185→│  Öffentl. WebRX  │◄──────────────────►│                  │
   186→│  (beliebig)      │   FFT (read-only)  │                  │
   187→└──────────────────┘                    └──────────────────┘
   188→```
   189→
   190→## Wie es funktioniert
   191→
   192→1. **WebSocket-Verbindung**: BandWacht verbindet sich zum OpenWebRX-Server über den gleichen WebSocket-Endpunkt, den auch der Browser nutzt (`ws://host:port/ws/`)
   193→
   194→2. **FFT-Daten empfangen**: Der Server sendet komprimierte FFT-Spektrumdaten (ADPCM) die das gesamte sichtbare Band darstellen
   195→
   196→3. **Spektrumanalyse**: Die FFT-Daten werden dekomprimiert und auf definierte Frequenzbereiche analysiert. Ein adaptiver Noise-Floor-Schätzer vermeidet Fehlalarme.
   197→
   198→4. **Carrier-Erkennung**: Signale über dem Schwellwert (absolut oder relativ zum Noise Floor) lösen nach einer Haltezeit Events aus
   199→
   200→5. **Benachrichtigung & Aufnahme**: Events werden an konfigurierte Backends gesendet und optional wird Audio aufgenommen

200→5. **Benachrichtigung & Aufnahme**: Events werden an konfigurierte Backends gesendet und optional wird Audio aufgenommen
   201→
   202→## Einschränkungen
   203→
   204→- **Ein Slot pro Verbindung**: Jede WebSocket-Verbindung belegt einen Client-Slot am Server
   205→- **Profil-Wechsel**: BandWacht kann das Profil (Band) am Server umschalten (`--profile`), aber der SDR kann nur ein Band gleichzeitig empfangen
   206→- **Audio-Aufnahme limitiert**: Audio wird nur für die aktuell eingestellte Demodulator-Frequenz empfangen (Limitation von OpenWebRX)
   207→- **Öffentliche Server**: Können jederzeit offline gehen oder die Konfiguration ändern
   208→
   209→## Web UI
   210→
   211→BandWacht enthält eine vollständige Web-Oberfläche zur Live-Überwachung, Konfiguration und Ereignishistorie.
   212→
   213→### Features
   214→
   215→- **Live-Spektrum**: Echtzeit-FFT-Darstellung im Browser (Canvas-basiert)
   216→- **Dashboard**: SDR-Instanzen starten/stoppen, Live-Ereignis-Feed
   217→- **Konfiguration**: SDR-Instanzen, Überwachungsziele, Erkennungsparameter, Benachrichtigungen
   218→- **Logbuch**: Paginierte Ereignishistorie mit Filtern, CSV-Export, Audio-Wiedergabe
   219→- **Statistiken**: Häufigste Frequenzen, tägliche/wöchentliche Übersicht (Recharts)
   220→- **Responsive**: Desktop + Mobile, dunkles SDR-Theme
   221→
   222→### Architektur
   223→
   224→```
   225→Browser (React + Vite + Tailwind)
   226→    │
   227→    ├── REST API ──► FastAPI Backend
   228→    │                   ├── MonitorManager (wraps BandWacht engine)
   229→    │                   ├── SQLite via async SQLAlchemy
   230→    │                   └── Serves built frontend as static files
   231→    │
   232→    └── WebSocket ◄── /ws/spectrum/{id} (live FFT) + /ws/events (detections)
   233→```
   234→
   235→### Web UI starten (Entwicklung)
   236→
   237→```bash
   238→# Backend
   239→cd web/backend && pip install -r requirements.txt
   240→uvicorn web.backend.main:app --reload
   241→
   242→# Frontend (separates Terminal)
   243→cd web/frontend && npm install && npm run dev
   244→```
   245→
   246→### Web UI deployen (Docker)
   247→
   248→```bash
   249→# .env.production konfigurieren
   250→cp .env.production.example .env.production
   251→# Werte anpassen (DEPLOY_HOST, REMOTE_DIR, etc.)
   252→
   253→# Deployment
   254→./deploy-bandwacht-web.sh
   255→```
   256→
   257→Die Web UI läuft als eigenständiger Docker-Container (Port 3418) und ist unter https://bandwacht.oeradio.at erreichbar.
   258→
   259→### API Endpunkte
   260→
   261→| Endpunkt | Beschreibung |
   262→|----------|-------------|
   263→| `GET/POST /api/v1/instances` | SDR-Instanzen CRUD |
   264→| `POST /api/v1/instances/{id}/start\|stop` | Monitor starten/stoppen |
   265→| `GET/POST /api/v1/targets` | Überwachungsziele CRUD |
   266→| `GET /api/v1/events` | Ereignisse (paginiert, filterbar) |
   267→| `GET /api/v1/events/export` | CSV-Export |
   268→| `GET /api/v1/recordings/{file}` | WAV-Aufnahmen streamen |
   269→| `GET/PUT /api/v1/settings` | Erkennungsparameter |
   270→| `WS /ws/spectrum/{id}` | Live FFT-Daten (~10fps) |
   271→| `WS /ws/events` | Live Erkennungs-Events |
   272→
   273→## Integration mit FunkPilot
   274→
   275→BandWacht ist als Modul für das FunkPilot-Ökosystem konzipiert:
   276→
   277→- **relaisblick**: Liefert Repeater-Frequenzen als Watch-Targets
   278→- **FunkPilot API**: Events können an die FunkPilot-API gesendet werden

class TelegramNotification(NotificationBackend):
    """Send notifications via Telegram Bot."""

    def __init__(self, bot_token: str, chat_id: str):
        self.bot_token = bot_token
        self.chat_id = chat_id

    async def send(self, event: DetectionEvent) -> bool:
        try:
            import aiohttp
            freq_mhz = event.freq_hz / 1e6
            label = f" [{event.target_label}]" if event.target_label else ""
            text = (
                f"📡 *Träger erkannt*{label}\n"
                f"Frequenz: `{freq_mhz:.4f}` MHz\n"
                f"Peak: `{event.peak_db:.1f}` dB\n"
                f"Zeit: {event.timestamp.strftime('%H:%M:%S %Z')}"
            )
            async with aiohttp.ClientSession() as session:

## Investigation Report: Telegram Notifications Not Working in BandWacht

Based on my thorough investigation of the BandWacht codebase, I have identified **the root cause and multiple contributing factors** preventing Telegram notifications from working. Here are my findings:

### CRITICAL ISSUE #1: Missing Environment Variables in Docker Deployment

**Location:** `/home/achildrenmile/bandwacht/docker-compose.web.yml` (lines 13-16)

**The Problem:**
The `docker-compose.web.yml` file does NOT include any `BANDWACHT_NOTIFY_*` environment variables. The file only passes:
- `BANDWACHT_DATABASE_URL`
- `BANDWACHT_RECORDINGS_DIR`
- `BANDWACHT_CORS_ORIGINS`

This is the **primary reason** Telegram notifications stopped working after commit 59fcdd2. The code now requires environment variables instead of database configuration.

**What's Missing:**
```yaml
# These are NOT in the docker-compose.web.yml:
- BANDWACHT_NOTIFY_TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN=<your-token>
- BANDWACHT_NOTIFY_TELEGRAM_CHAT_ID=<your-chat-id>
- BANDWACHT_NOTIFY_GOTIFY_URL=...
- BANDWACHT_NOTIFY_GOTIFY_TOKEN=...
- BANDWACHT_NOTIFY_NTFY_TOPIC=...
- BANDWACHT_NOTIFY_WEBHOOK_URL=...
```

### CRITICAL ISSUE #2: Incomplete Migration in Commit 59fcdd2

**Location:** Commit `59fcdd2 "Move notification config from DB/UI to environment variables"`

**Details of the Change:**
The commit successfully:
1. Added `notify_*` fields to `web/backend/config.py` (lines 16-23)
2. Created `configured_notifications()` method to read from env vars
3. Updated `monitor_manager.py` to instantiate notifiers from env vars
4. Modified the notification API endpoint to be read-only

**What Was Missed:**
- NO DOCUMENTATION about how to configure environment variables in docker-compose
- NO MIGRATION GUIDE for existing deployments
- NO DEFAULT VALUES for Telegram configuration
- The deployment script (`deploy-bandwacht-web.sh`) was not updated to handle notification env vars

### Code Flow Analysis: How Telegram Notifications Are Built

**File:** `/home/achildrenmile/bandwacht/web/backend/services/monitor_manager.py` (lines 198-202)

```python
if app_settings.notify_telegram_bot_token and app_settings.notify_telegram_chat_id:
    notifiers.append(TelegramNotification(
        bot_token=app_settings.notify_telegram_bot_token,
        chat_id=app_settings.notify_telegram_chat_id,
    ))
```

**The Check:** Both `notify_telegram_bot_token` AND `notify_telegram_chat_id` must be non-empty strings.

**Default Values:** `/home/achildrenmile/bandwacht/web/backend/config.py` (lines 19-20)
```python
notify_telegram_bot_token: str = ""
notify_telegram_chat_id: str = ""
```

Both default to empty strings, so if environment variables aren't set, Telegram won't be configured.

### Issue #3: Telegram API Call Implementation

**File:** `/home/achildrenmile/bandwacht/bandwacht.py` (lines 266-296)

The `TelegramNotification` class implementation looks correct:
- Uses `aiohttp` to call Telegram Bot API
- Endpoint: `https://api.telegram.org/bot{bot_token}/sendMessage`
- Sends text with Markdown formatting
- Returns `resp.status == 200`

**Potential Issues:**
1. If `chat_id` is an integer instead of string in env var, it would still work (passed as param)
2. If `bot_token` is invalid, the API call will fail silently (caught in exception handler)

### Configuration Detection System

**File:** `/home/achildrenmile/bandwacht/web/backend/config.py` (lines 43-54)

The `configured_notifications()` method returns which backends are available:

```python
def configured_notifications(self) -> list[dict]:
    """Return list of notification backends configured via env vars."""
    result = [{"backend": "console", "enabled": True, "configured": True}]
    if self.notify_gotify_url and self.notify_gotify_token:
        result.append({"backend": "gotify", "enabled": True, "configured": True})
    if self.notify_telegram_bot_token and self.notify_telegram_chat_id:
        result.append({"backend": "telegram", "enabled": True, "configured": True})
    # ... rest
```

Since both Telegram env vars default to empty strings, the method will NOT list Telegram as configured.

### API Notification Test Endpoint

**File:** `/home/achildrenmile/bandwacht/web/backend/routers/notifications.py` (lines 15-25)

The test endpoint checks if backend is in the configured list:
```python
@router.post("/notifications/{backend}/test")
async def test_notification(backend: str):
    configured = {n["backend"] for n in settings.configured_notifications()}
    if backend not in configured:
        raise HTTPException(404, f"Backend '{backend}' ist nicht konfiguriert")
    
    from ..services.monitor_manager import manager
    success = await manager.test_notification(backend)
    if not success:
        raise HTTPException(500, "Testbenachrichtigung fehlgeschlagen")
    return {"ok": True, "message": "Testbenachrichtigung gesendet"}
```

If Telegram env vars aren't set, the test endpoint will return 404.

### Summary of Root Causes

1. **Primary:** `docker-compose.web.yml` missing `BANDWACHT_NOTIFY_TELEGRAM_*` environment variables
2. **Secondary:** No deployment documentation for environment variable setup
3. **Tertiary:** Empty defaults mean Telegram won't initialize even if code runs
4. **Quaternary:** No error logging to indicate why Telegram isn't configured

### What Needs to Be Done

To fix Telegram notifications, the deployment must:

1. Add environment variables to `docker-compose.web.yml`:
   ```yaml
   environment:
     - BANDWACHT_NOTIFY_TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN=<bot-token>
     - BANDWACHT_NOTIFY_TELEGRAM_CHAT_ID=<chat-id>
   ```

2. OR add them to the `.env.production` file and pass them to docker-compose

3. Verify the values are being read:
   - Check if `BANDWACHT_NOTIFY_TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN` env var is set
   - Check if `BANDWACHT_NOTIFY_TELEGRAM_CHAT_ID` env var is set
   - These should NOT be empty strings

4. Test via the notification API endpoint that Telegram is in the configured list

### File Structure Summary

**Key Files Involved:**
- `/home/achildrenmile/bandwacht/web/backend/config.py` — Configuration via env vars
- `/home/achildrenmile/bandwacht/web/backend/routers/notifications.py` — REST API endpoint
- `/home/achildrenmile/bandwacht/web/backend/services/monitor_manager.py` — Notifier instantiation (lines 198-202)
- `/home/achildrenmile/bandwacht/bandwacht.py` — TelegramNotification class (lines 266-296)
- `/home/achildrenmile/bandwacht/docker-compose.web.yml` — **MISSING env vars**
- `/home/achildrenmile/bandwacht/deploy-bandwacht-web.sh` — Deployment script (no notification config)

The architecture is sound, but the deployment configuration was not updated to match the new environment variable requirement.

services:
  bandwacht-web:
    build:
      context: .
      dockerfile: web/Dockerfile.web
    container_name: bandwacht-web
    restart: unless-stopped
    ports:

      - BANDWACHT_DATABASE_URL=sqlite+aiosqlite:////app/data/bandwacht_web.db

      - BANDWACHT_CORS_ORIGINS=${CORS_ORIGIN:-https://bandwacht.oeradio.at}
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "curl -sf http://localhost:8000/api/v1/health || exit 1"]
      interval: 30s
      timeout: 10s
      retries: 3
      start_period: 15s
    networks:
      - cloudflared-tunnel

volumes:
  bandwacht-data:
    driver: local
  bandwacht-recordings:
    driver: local

#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -e

# Colors for output
RED='\033[0;31m'
GREEN='\033[0;32m'
YELLOW='\033[1;33m'
NC='\033[0m' # No Color

# Load environment variables
if [ -f ".env.production" ]; then
    source .env.production
else
    echo -e "${RED}Error: .env.production file not found${NC}"
    echo "Copy .env.production.example to .env.production and configure it"
    exit 1
fi

# Validate required variables
REQUIRED_VARS="DEPLOY_HOST REMOTE_DIR CONTAINER_NAME IMAGE_NAME CONTAINER_PORT SITE_URL"
for var in $REQUIRED_VARS; do
    if [ -z "${!var}" ]; then
        echo -e "${RED}Error: $var is not set in .env.production${NC}"
        exit 1
    fi
done

# Check for --rebuild flag
REBUILD_FLAG=""
if [ "$1" == "--rebuild" ]; then
    REBUILD_FLAG="--no-cache"
    echo -e "${YELLOW}Rebuild flag set — will build without cache${NC}"
fi

echo -e "${GREEN}=== Deploying BandWacht Web to $DEPLOY_HOST ===${NC}"
echo "Host: $DEPLOY_HOST"
echo "Remote dir: $REMOTE_DIR"
echo "Container: $CONTAINER_NAME"
echo "Port: $CONTAINER_PORT"
echo ""

# Step 1: Sync code to remote host
echo -e "${GREEN}Step 1: Syncing code...${NC}"
GIT_URL=$(git remote get-url origin 2>/dev/null || echo "")
ssh "$DEPLOY_HOST" "
    if [ -d '$REMOTE_DIR' ]; then
        cd '$REMOTE_DIR' && git pull
    else
        mkdir -p '$(dirname $REMOTE_DIR)'
        git clone '$GIT_URL' '$REMOTE_DIR'
    fi
"

# Step 2: Build Docker image on remote
echo -e "${GREEN}Step 2: Building Docker image...${NC}"
ssh "$DEPLOY_HOST" "
    cd '$REMOTE_DIR'
    docker build $REBUILD_FLAG -t '$IMAGE_NAME' -f web/Dockerfile.web .
"

# Step 3: Restart container (volumes are preserved — data persists)
echo -e "${GREEN}Step 3: Restarting container...${NC}"
ssh "$DEPLOY_HOST" "
    cd '$REMOTE_DIR'
    docker compose -f docker-compose.web.yml up -d --force-recreate --build
"

# Step 4: Verify deployment
echo -e "${GREEN}Step 4: Verifying deployment...${NC}"
sleep 3

# Check container status
CONTAINER_STATUS=$(ssh "$DEPLOY_HOST" "docker ps --filter 'name=$CONTAINER_NAME' --format '{{.Status}}'")
echo "Container status: $CONTAINER_STATUS"

# Check local port
LOCAL_PORT=$(echo $CONTAINER_PORT | cut -d: -f1)
if ssh "$DEPLOY_HOST" "curl -sf -o /dev/null http://localhost:$LOCAL_PORT/api/v1/health"; then
    echo -e "${GREEN}✓ Container is running on port $LOCAL_PORT${NC}"
else
    echo -e "${YELLOW}⚠ Container not yet responding on port $LOCAL_PORT — may still be starting${NC}"
fi

# Check public URL
if curl -sf -o /dev/null "$SITE_URL" 2>/dev/null; then
    echo -e "${GREEN}✓ Site is accessible at $SITE_URL${NC}"
else
    echo -e "${YELLOW}⚠ Public URL not yet accessible — configure Cloudflare tunnel${NC}"
fi

echo ""
echo -e "${GREEN}=== Deployment complete ===${NC}"

# BandWacht Project Memory

## Deployment
- Deploy via `bash deploy-bandwacht-web.sh` (sources `.env.production`, SSHs to `host-node-01`)
- Docker compose at `docker-compose.web.yml`, container runs on port 3418 internally mapped to 8000
- `.env.production` is gitignored — contains deploy host config + secrets (Telegram tokens, etc.)
- Docker compose reads `.env` on the remote host for `BANDWACHT_*` env vars
- `--rebuild` flag forces `--no-cache` on docker build but Docker may still cache layers if the requirements.txt hasn't changed content

## Known Issues
- `passlib` 1.7.4 is incompatible with `bcrypt` 5.x — pin `bcrypt>=4.0,<5` in requirements.txt
- When moving config from DB to env vars, MUST also update docker-compose.web.yml to forward the new env vars
